gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the 'Reolink Go Series G440' card ChatGPT showed (Best Buy) is the same camera as the Reolink Go PT Ultra, or that the 'G430' is the Go PT Plus. Reolink's own US SIM article lists them as one model each ('Reolink Go PT Ultra, Go Series G440'; 'Reolink Go PT Plus, Go Series G430'). The same article recommends T-Mobile prepaid data-only SIMs for SIMs the buyer supplies, plus Mint and FreedomPop. For Verizon it only says to test a SIM you already have before activating a new one.
standout_why: Pages compared: reolink.com/us Go PT Ultra page (cited), homesecurityradar.com security-cameras-without-wifi, and smarthomeexplorer.com best-cellular-lte guide. None of them maps G440 to Go PT Ultra or G430 to Go PT Plus. ChatGPT's own answers treat them as different products at different prices: Go PT Ultra at $159.99 (B&H) or '$230–$280', and G440 at $189.99 or $209.99. homesecurityradar already says Reolink recommends T-Mobile and AT&T prepaid plans plus FreedomPop and Mint. That part is only partly new. No rival quotes Reolink's 'Verizon: test it first' wording. No rival notes that Reolink's own product page names Verizon for the bundled SIM but leaves Verizon off its carrier table for SIMs you buy yourself. smarthomeexplorer cites only a Slickdeals user who says the S330 'only works with the EIOT sim'. eufy's own page says the opposite ('Your own nano SIM also works with a data-only plan').
decides: This confirms the Go PT Ultra as a true 4G-only pick (Reolink: 'does not support WiFi'). The page can tell shoppers that the Go PT Ultra and the G440 are one camera, so they compare prices across both names instead of buying the 'cheaper alternative'. It also gives a carrier rule. If Verizon is the only signal at the site, use the SIM that comes in the box with the Reolink, or choose the eufy S330. eufy's page lists Verizon for its included EIOTCLUB SIM and allows your own data-only nano SIM. Reolink does not list Verizon for a SIM you buy yourself.
